newsitem.title: POLAND: Small Prague gains lead East European markets.
newsitem.headline: Small Prague gains lead East European markets.

text.p: The Prague bourse rose slightly this week, while profit-taking knocked Budapest and Warsaw off their recent record highs.
Foreign buying spurred Slovenian shares, Romanian shares stayed strong, Croatian stocks were mixed, and the Slovak bourse eased.
The CESI Central European Share Index fell 16.13 points or one percent, on the week to 1,610.33 points.
PRAGUE

Major Czech issues drifted in directionless trade, but rises on the broader market helped the PX50 to another small gain in the week to Thursday. The PX50 rose 5.2 points, or 0.9 percent, in the period to close on Thursday at 562.7.
The highest capitalised stock, SPT Telecom, which has oscillated around the 3,400 crown mark for several weeks gained 15 crowns over the week to 3,385.
Dealers say they have been expecting a wave of foreign buying to boost blue chips but it had failed to materialise.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian shares fell this week after rising about 30 percent this year. The BUX index closing on Thursday at 5,333.18 points, down two percent from last Friday.
Leading stocks began to fall at the beginning of the week as investors decided to cash in profits.
Traders said profit-taking was likely continue, but that the market's direction would be determined by 1996 corporate results to be published by February 15.
The market is particularly looking forward to the results of oil stock MOL, the chemicals makers and the drugs producers.
"If these results are good, as expected, then the (declining) trend will reverse," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft.
WARSAW
Polish shares fell in profit-taking this week after reaching successive 33-month highs and analysts said they expected the market to fall again on Friday.
"The fall could continue to about 16,000 points...with tomorrow's fall smaller than today's," said Maciej Matusiak, of PKO BP brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed at 16,167.9 points on Thursday, down 460.2 points or 2.8 percent from last Friday's close.
Bank stocks were particularly hurt this week after the central bank's decision on Monday to raise mandatory reserves on deposits. Most banks either slowed their falls or rebounded on Thursday.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares jumped 2.74 percent this week on heavy foreign buying. The 10-share SBI index soared 40.6 points to 1,520.0. Total turnover was 3.4 billion tolars ($22.8 million).
Construction firm GPG was the top gainer, up 27.9 percent, while the biggest loser was financial consultancy Primofin, down 21.1 percent.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks ended mixed on Thursday, with a slight correction among blue chips and gains for hoteliers, and were seen moving up further in the coming days but at a slower pace.
Food processor Podravka hit a record high of 375 kuna on Tuesday on news it had made good progress in restructuring. It closed at 330 kuna on Thursday, 30 above its nominal value.

Traders expected and even welcomed a correction of the leading Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva after their steep rise in 1997. Pliva closed at 502 kuna, down 11 from last week. Zagrebacka ended at 1,900 kuna, up 30 from last Friday.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange continued trading sluggishly this week, with the 12-share SAX index sliding 1.04 points to 186.38 on Thursday from Monday's opening.
Brokers said the market now looked undervalued and they expected low prices to attract more foreign investors in coming weeks.

"Prices have fallen to attractive levels, and we think that those investors now focusing on Poland, Hungary or Russia may turn their attention to Slovakia when those markets stop their current growth," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
BUCHAREST
The market's bull run pushing two unofficial indices to year highs this week but began to wane on Thursday, with investors focusing on few stocks.
Thursday's turnover of 802.9 million lei was this year's highest and the second highest ever.

Azomures fertiliser maker, which moved to the first tier this week, took the bulk of turnover from cross trades and a special deal struck outside the market on Thursday. It closed 3,300 lei stronger on the week at 24,000.
